answer.label: Not Harry S. Truman — a fabricated telegram
answer.authorName: No verified author — an anonymous internet joke
answer.authorDates: Credited to Harry S. Truman (1884–1972), 33rd U.S. president — via telegrams that do not exist
answer.sourceLine: The line reaches most people inside a chain e-mail reproducing four telegrams supposedly sent between Truman, Douglas MacArthur and Chester Nimitz on 1 September 1945. The Harry S. Truman Library & Museum states plainly that the exchange “does not exist at the Truman Library” ↗. The sentence itself is an anonymous internet joke about political correctness that was already circulating in December 2006 — it was retrofitted onto Truman in 2015.
answer.confidenceText: Disputed — the telegrams are fabricated, and the sentence is an anonymous joke with no known author.

source.heading: The “source” that does not exist

source.excerpt:
(3) Tokyo, Japan — 1630, September 1, 1945. To: H S Truman. From: D A MacArthur and C H Nimitz. Wilco Sir, but both Chester and I are somewhat confused, exactly what does the term politically correct mean?

(4) Washington, D C — 2120, September 1, 1945. To: D A MacArthur/C H Nimitz. From: H S Truman. Political Correctness is a doctrine, recently fostered by a delusional, illogical minority and promoted by a sick mainstream media, which holds forth the proposition that it is entirely possible to pick up a piece of shit by clean end!
trail: The Harry S. Truman Library & Museum answers this one directly: the purported exchange “does not exist at the Truman Library,” and Chester Nimitz’s middle initial is W, not H ↗. The National Archives’ own Our Presidents blog said the same when the e-mail began arriving in its inbox.

Snopes rated the telegram story False on 8 April 2015 ↗, reporting that evidence of the exchange was virtually non-existent online before 2015, and tracing versions of the joke itself to 2006 and 2007, attributed at least twice to students of Texas A&M University.

The oldest dated copy located here is a blog post of 7 December 2006 ↗, forwarded from a reader, with “liberal minority,” “liberal press” and “turd by the clean end” — and no president anywhere in it.
By February 2012 the sentence was in print with its modern wording, quoted by a Townhall columnist as “an old Internet joke” ↗ — three years before the Truman telegrams surfaced.
source.excerptNote: Reproduced from Snopes’s transcription of the chain e-mail ↗. These telegrams are not archival documents; the Truman Library says they do not exist, and the misspelled initial — Chester W. Nimitz — is one of the tells.

author.name: Harry S. Truman
author.kicker: The man it is pinned on
author.heading: About Harry S. Truman
author.bio: Harry S. Truman took office in April 1945 and was president when Japan surrendered that September — which is exactly why the forged telegrams are set on 1 September 1945. He was famously blunt, and that reputation is the whole engine of the hoax: a crude one-liner sounds like something he might have snapped. But the phrase “mainstream media” is a much later coinage, and the modern sense of “political correctness” only entered wide circulation in the campus debates of the late 1980s — decades after the date on the telegram. Nothing in Truman’s papers contains this sentence.

misattribution.heading: Where this one went wrong
misattribution.intro: Three separate claims travel with this quotation, and all three fail: the telegrams, the contest, and the wording itself.

items.who: Harry S. Truman, Douglas MacArthur and Chester Nimitz
items.why: The Harry S. Truman Library & Museum states the purported exchange “does not exist at the Truman Library” ↗, notes that Nimitz’s middle initial is W rather than the H used in the e-mail, and observes that the messages suggest a familiarity between Truman and MacArthur that did not exist. TruthOrFiction was told the same thing by the library.

The joke’s earlier life came with a different credit: rec.humor.funny’s archive calls it “the 2007 winning entry from an annual contest at Texas A&M University” ↗. Snopes notes the line was attributed at least twice to Texas A&M students but calls the joke’s origins murky — no such contest result has ever been produced.

The Truman version’s “recently fostered … a sick mainstream media … a piece of shit by clean end” is a reworking. The 2006 text reads “a delusional illogical liberal minority & rabidly promoted by an unscrupulous liberal press … a turd by the clean end” ↗.

misattribution.truthLine: The sentence is an anonymous internet joke with no identified author, in circulation by December 2006 and quoted in print as “an old Internet joke” ↗ in February 2012 — years before anyone attached Harry Truman’s name to it.

context.heading: Why the forgery falls apart on its own words
lead: The chain e-mail is unusually specific — four telegrams, each with a city, a timestamp and a sender — and that specificity is what sinks it. It has President Truman warning MacArthur that his remarks are “not politically correct,” then explaining the term to two officers who supposedly had never heard it. Snopes points out that the reply uses mainstream media, a partisan coinage of a much later era, and that the modern sense of political correctness only spread through American campus debates from the late 1980s. The Truman Library adds a detail no forger thought to check: the admiral’s middle initial is W, not H ↗.

Strip the telegrams away and what remains is a joke with its own paper trail. In December 2006 it circulated as a definition credited vaguely to “students at Texas A&M University”; by 2008 the rec.humor.funny archive was presenting it as the winning entry in a Texas A&M definitions contest — a framing nobody has ever verified, and one that follows the familiar shape of an e-mail forward inventing a contest to lend itself authority. In 2012 a Townhall columnist quoted it, accurately, as “an old Internet joke” ↗. Only afterwards did somebody bolt a president onto it.
context.detailsSummary: How the wording changed on its way to Truman
detailsBody: December 2006 — “a doctrine fostered by a delusional illogical liberal minority & rabidly promoted by an unscrupulous liberal press … pick up a turd by the clean end,” credited to students at Texas A&M.
By 2008 — “fostered by a delusional, illogical minority, and rabidly promoted by an unscrupulous mainstream media … pick up a turd by the clean end,” presented as a 2007 contest winner.
2012 — quoted in print as an old internet joke, now with “pick up a piece of shit by the clean end.”
2015 — the same sentence appears inside four invented telegrams, reworded to “recently fostered … promoted by a sick mainstream media … by clean end,” and signed H. S. Truman.
context.pull: An anonymous joke acquired a president — roughly nine years after it started circulating without one.

sourcesVerified.claim: The Harry S. Truman Library & Museum states the purported Truman–MacArthur telegram exchange does not exist at the library, that Chester Nimitz's middle initial is W not H, that the telegrams contain terms such as "mainstream media" that did not exist in Truman's time, and that they imply a camaraderie between MacArthur and Truman that did not exist.

Snopes, in a fact check published 8 April 2015 by Kim LaCapria, rated the claim False, reproduced all four purported telegrams including the wording "pick up a piece of shit by clean end", said evidence of the exchange was virtually non-existent online before 2015, and noted versions of the joke dating to 2006 and 2007 attributed at least twice to students of Texas A&M University.

A blog post dated 7 December 2006 carries the definition as "Political Correctness is a doctrine fostered by a delusional illogical liberal minority & rabidly promoted by an unscrupulous liberal press which holds forth the proposition that it is entirely possible to pick up a turd by the clean end," noting it "has been attributed to students at Texas A&M University."

The rec.humor.funny joke archive presents the line as "the 2007 winning entry from an annual contest at Texas A&M University calling for the most appropriate definition of a contemporary term," with the wording "unscrupulous mainstream media" and "pick up a turd by the clean end."

Gary Shapiro's Townhall column of 16 February 2012, "Political Correctness is Hurting America," introduces the line as "an old Internet joke" and quotes it with the wording "pick up a piece of shit by the clean end."

The National Archives' Our Presidents blog states that the widely circulated e-mail claiming a Truman-MacArthur telegram exchange is false, that the e-mail's claim the telegrams are at the Truman Library is not true, that archivists are unaware of any such telegrams, and that the "telegrams" contain terms such as "mainstream media" not in use in Truman's time.

TruthOrFiction rated the chain e-mail Fiction and reported that the Harry S. Truman Library & Museum told them the correspondence does "not exist in the library's holdings," and that the e-mail gets Chester W. Nimitz's middle initial wrong.

English Wikiquote's Harry S. Truman page has Disputed and Misattributed sections but contains no entry for this political-correctness line, no mention of "clean end," and no telegram exchange with MacArthur on the subject.
